title: Loops
short: for over a range, enumerate, zip, while, break and continue.
what: A loop runs the same lines once per item. for walks over anything you can list: a range of numbers, a list, a string. while keeps going as long as a condition is true.
analogy: Checking tickets at a door. for: take each person in the line in turn. while: keep checking until the hall is full.

frames.label: for i in range(len(nums))
frames.say: range(len(nums)) counts 0, 1, 2, 3, 4: one index per cell. It stops before 5, so i never runs off the end.

frames.label: if nums[i] % 2 == 1: continue
frames.say: i = 1 reads 7, which is odd. continue skips the rest of this turn and jumps to the next i.

frames.label: if nums[i] % 2 == 1: continue
frames.say: After the loop, the even values 4, 2 and 6 were printed. The odd ones were skipped by continue.

frames.label: for i, x in enumerate(nums)
frames.say: enumerate hands you the index and the value together. break leaves the loop at the first x above 8.

frames.label: for a, b in zip(nums, nums[1:])
frames.say: zip(a, b) walks two lists side by side. zip(nums, nums[1:]) pairs each item with its right neighbour, like (7, 2).

frames.label: for i in range(4, -1, -1)
frames.say: reversed(nums) walks from the back. range(4, -1, -1) gives 4, 3, 2, 1, 0: the middle -1 means stop after 0.

frames.label: while left < right
frames.say: while repeats until its condition is false. Good when the step is not one-by-one, like two pointers closing in.

frames.label: while left < right
frames.say: Each turn moves left up and right down. At left = 2, right = 2, left < right is false, so the loop ends.

when: Need the index and the value
Compare each item with its neighbour
Two pointers moving toward each other
watch: range(a, b) stops before b: range(1, 5) is 1, 2, 3, 4.
zip stops at the shorter list without any warning.
A while loop that never moves its pointer runs forever.
